items.title: Pay disputed collection demand
items.quote: Der Betrag ist binnen 4 Tagen, das heißt bis spätestens 11.04.2025, auf das Sonderkonto IBAN SK20 1100 0000 0029 4512 3456 (Empfänger: R. Horváth, Verwendungszweck ZFB-25-0407-118) zu überweisen.
items.computation: The letter itself states an explicit calendar due date ('bis spätestens 11.04.2025') rather than only a period, so this date is used as written. 11.04.2025 falls on a Friday (letter dated Mon 07.04.2025; today given as Wed 09.04.2025), a regular working day in NW, so no weekend/holiday shift applies even though this is a private (non-authority) demand.

warnings: This has strong hallmarks of a scam/predatory debt-collection letter: an unusually short 4-day payment deadline, threats of immediate wage garnishment and credit-bureau entries without any prior court judgment, and a foreign (Slovak) IBAN with a personal (not company) account holder name for payment of a German consumer debt.

The claim that 'Einwände gegen die Forderung werden nicht mehr bearbeitet' (objections will no longer be processed) has no legal basis — a debtor always retains the right to dispute a claim; this looks like an intimidation tactic.

A genuine 'Vollstreckungsbescheid' (enforcement order) can only be obtained after a court-run Mahnverfahren (dunning procedure) with prior notice to the debtor, not simply 'announced' by a private collection agency without further process — this threat should be treated with suspicion.

No documentation of the underlying 'Glücksmuster Premium' subscription contract (date signed, terms, prior invoices) is provided; verify the existence and amount of the underlying debt with the original creditor before paying anything.

Do not transfer money to the given IBAN without independently verifying the legitimacy of this claim and the collection agency, e.g. via a consumer protection agency (Verbraucherzentrale) or a lawyer.
